label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They appear to be psychologically well-adjusted, with UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below typical thresholds, near-minimal depression on the PHQ-9, and virtually negligible anxiety on the GAD-7. Their moderate daily screen or online engagement (1–3 hours) suggests balanced digital habits rather than excessive or avoidant use.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily online/screen time
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores indicating strong social connectedness
Near-floor depressive symptom levels suggesting stable mood
Moderate and controlled daily screen/online usage (1–3 hours)
Higher educational attainment potentially linked to greater coping resources

label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.69) and depression scores (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.68) are above moderate thresholds, while their anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.15) are notably the highest among the measured indicators, suggesting a pronounced pattern of psychological distress co-occurring with heavy digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Exhibits the highest distress on anxiety measures (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.15)
Engages in prolonged daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
Represents a sizable subgroup (n = 178) within the training sample
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of multiple psychological risk indicators in a high-screen-time, highly educated female population

label: Emotionally Resilient Graduate-Educated Woman
summary: This profile represents women with graduate-level education who spend a moderate amount of time (1–3 hours) online and report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of approximately 1.22, a PHQ-9 depression mean of approximately 0.82, and a GAD-7 anxiety mean of approximately 0.83—all near the bottom of their respective scales—these respondents exhibit strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily internet/social media use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness, scoring well below midpoint on the UCLA-8 scale
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology as measured by the PHQ-9
Demonstrates negligible anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7
Maintains moderate and bounded daily internet or social media usage (1–3 hours)
Represents a sizable subgroup (n=339), suggesting this is a common and stable well-being pattern among highly educated women
tone: Calm, stable, and psychologically grounded with an overall sense of emotional equilibrium
